Someone finally gets it. It's been almost a year in the making, stripped upper and lower assembled piece by piece. 18" barrel, rifle length gas chambered in .223 Wylde chopped to 16" with some gas port work. Let's hope she cycles!

Why didn't you just build a mock dissipator? You could have his a carbine length gas system under the handguard. Let us know how it cycles. I don't think I've ever seen a real Dissy. My carbine has hand guard envy.

I was looking for a more challenging build. While the carbine is considered to be the most reliable gas system due to the overgassed bolt carrier group, you get increased (read: accelerated) wear on your internals. Right now they've got all kinds of "band aids" to slow down the bolt carrier group (eg. heavy buffers, recoil springs) I don't like band aid fixes, I'd much rather have a "perfectly gassed" system from the get-go. Granted, I understand that there are certain trade offs when it comes to choosing one gas system over another, I just wanted to try to do something different.

On the subject of handguard envy, I really want the Magpul MOE SL handguard. They gauged interest with the carbine length first, and they just started shipping the mid length handguards. Still waiting for my rifle length SL furniture.

https://www.magpul.com/products/moe-sl-hand-guard-mid-length
Neat.Id be worried about undergassing it though. let us know how it runs.

I'll be honest with you, I'm a bit on edge as well. I went into this build half expecting to have to remove the front sight post for more gas port work. But I got my numbers from a reputable source. I keep telling myself that to try to keep my mind at ease. "I've seen his rifle cycle flawlessly with these numbers, why shouldn't mine?"

I'll be visiting a friend tomorrow to double and triple check headspace during my lunch break. If all goes well, I should have her on the range tomorrow night after work.

Alrighty voaters! The jury is in! Here are today's results!

6 rounds fired @ 30 feet (10 yards or 9.144 m just in case anyone in EU decides to check out v/guns) I just wanted to make sure I would even hit the paper. Then 6 more rounds @ 75 feet (25 yards, 22.86 m)

https://slimgur.com/image/AzD

3 rounds, adjust, 3 rounds, adjust, 3 rounds ZEROED

https://slimgur.com/image/AzH

3 more on a virgin target for good measure (and for my aesthetic pleasure)

https://slimgur.com/image/Az2

The pictures were uploaded from my cell phone (Samsung Galaxy S5) and no matter how many different directions I rotated the pictures in my photo studio, they still came out sideways or upside down when uploaded to Slimgur.

But yes! She cycles great! No feeding issues, no jamming, no extracting issues. I put 59 rounds through her (including the 24 used to zero, one got lost under a rag hence the odd number)

I am having one small trouble though, she's short cycling. Nothing I didn't expect. The bolt doesn't lock on an empty mag. Looks like I get to do a little more tinkering. This is my favorite part! She's most likely going to get a different buffer spring and possibly a lighter buffer. I plan on putting a few hundred more rounds through it first before I start to throw parts at it. I want to make sure everything is nice and slick, broken in, etc.

Latest update! Ran about 400 rounds through her with maybe 7 different styles/brands of magazines. I found that my IMI polymer mags were causing my bolt to not lock back on empty magazine intermittently. She's running like a champ, perfectly gassed and way less kick than a carbine. Add that in with the surefire muzzle brake and follow up shots are easier than ever to sight in.
